metadata.project: Blockchain-Based Provenance and Tamper-Evident Auditing for AI-Driven IoT Intrusion Detection

environment.note: Empirical synthesis of authoritative Phase 6A and Phase 6B experimental data.

research_question: Does blockchain-backed model provenance provide measurable authorization and auditability benefits beyond local SHA-256 integrity verification alone, at a quantified pre-load verification cost, while keeping blockchain operations outside the evaluated per-flow inference path?

configuration_a_ml_only.name: Configuration A (ML-Only Baseline)
configuration_a_ml_only.description: Standard Random Forest deployment without pre-load artifact integrity gates
capabilities_provided: Binary intrusion classification on 42 network-flow features
High baseline detection efficacy (90.30% Accuracy, 98.78% Precision, 92.41% F1)
Pure off-chain inference execution in server memory (42.40 ms mean)
security_omissions: No cryptographic artifact-integrity verification performed prior to model loading
No model provenance or version authorization registry consulted
Substituted or corrupted binary artifacts reach the loading path without detection
No operational security audit log of verification lifecycle

configuration_b_sha_only.name: Configuration B (SHA-256-Only Integrity Verification)
configuration_b_sha_only.description: Pre-load cryptographic integrity check using local SHA-256 against off-chain expected digest
capabilities_provided: Byte-exact local artifact integrity verification (5.65 ms mean)
Deterministic detection and rejection of binary modifications (HASH_MISMATCH)
Pre-load fail-closed behavior at the local application boundary
security_omissions: Expected digest is maintained off-chain without independent decentralized governance
Does not verify whether a specific model/version is officially authorized for release
If an attacker replaces the binary and updates the local expected hash, SHA-only accepts it
No immutable on-chain audit anchor or structured operational audit log

configuration_c_sha_blockchain.name: Configuration C (SHA-256 + Blockchain-Backed Provenance Verification)
configuration_c_sha_blockchain.description: Integrated architecture with local SHA-256 hashing, on-chain ModelRegistry, and fail-closed gate
capabilities_provided: All capabilities of Configuration A and Configuration B
On-chain model identity, version, algorithm, digest, and registrant authorization
Deterministic rejection of unregistered model/version identifiers (NOT_REGISTERED)
Fail-closed REST API gating (denies memory loading and returns HTTP 503 on predict)
Decoupled off-chain runtime inference (zero per-flow blockchain lookups)
Operational audit trail logging in SQLite with raw payload privacy protection
evaluated_tradeoff: Incurs a quantified pre-load verification cost (+14.66 ms incremental over SHA-only)
Requires smart contract deployment and local EVM interaction before model loading

ml_baseline.research_boundary: The blockchain and provenance registry layer does not replace the machine learning classifier and does not improve network-flow intrusion detection accuracy, precision, recall, or F1 score. The model weights and detection capabilities are completely identical across Configurations A, B, and C. The incremental value of the blockchain layer is strictly confined to pre-load artifact integrity, version authorization, fail-closed loading, and tamper-evident operational auditing.

provenance_comparison.config_a_action: No registry check exists in baseline
provenance_comparison.config_b_action: Provides local integrity comparison but no registry-membership check

derived_metrics.derivation_label: All derived quantities are calculated mathematically from directly measured empirical distributions.

security_matrix.config_a_ml_only: No artifact-integrity verification is performed in this baseline
security_matrix.config_b_sha_only: Rejected (Local SHA-256 mismatch detected in 13.66 ms)
security_matrix.config_c_sha_blockchain: Rejected (Fail-closed gate aborts loading; HTTP 503 enforced)

security_matrix.config_a_ml_only: No independent registry authorization performed in this baseline
security_matrix.config_b_sha_only: Digest can match caller expectation without release authorization
security_matrix.config_c_sha_blockchain: Rejected unless registered by designated governance authority
security_matrix.empirical_basis: Demonstrates distinction between integrity match and release authorization

security_matrix.config_a_ml_only: No provenance registry check exists in this baseline
security_matrix.config_b_sha_only: Provides local integrity comparison but no version-authorization check
security_matrix.empirical_basis: Empirically validated with unregistered version iot-ids-rf:v9.9.9

security_matrix.scenario_name: Model state in RAM after failed verification
security_matrix.config_a_ml_only: No verification gate present; loading proceeds unmonitored
security_matrix.config_b_sha_only: Application-level failure; memory loading aborted in verified path
security_matrix.config_c_sha_blockchain: Strictly fail-closed; memory remains unpopulated; predict blocked
security_matrix.empirical_basis: Validated in Experiment E6 and B4: is_loaded == False and HTTP 503

security_matrix.config_c_sha_blockchain: Yes (ModelRegistry.sol event ModelRegistered and state getModel)

security_matrix.scenario_name: Forensic audit logging of verification lifecycle
security_matrix.config_a_ml_only: No operational audit log evaluated in baseline
security_matrix.config_b_sha_only: No structured audit log evaluated in SHA-only baseline
security_matrix.config_c_sha_blockchain: Evaluated audit trail (SQLite WAL log, zero raw payload leakage)
security_matrix.empirical_basis: 10 security events audited (B10); verified 0 raw features persisted

verified_operational_facts.evaluated_inference_path: Local memory execution via scikit-learn / joblib pipeline

runtime_separation.architectural_claim: The evaluated pre-load verification operations are outside the per-flow inference path; no blockchain lookup or model re-hashing is performed during network-flow classification. This establishes architectural separation of the measured verification operations from the evaluated inference path, but it is not a controlled throughput measurement.

direct_measurements: Dataset SHA-256 hashes (training and testing CSVs)
Model artifact size (6,319,677 bytes) and SHA-256 (dc5e1688...)
ML evaluation metrics on N=175,341 test flows (Accuracy: 90.30%, Precision: 98.78%, Recall: 86.82%, F1: 92.41%)
Confusion matrix counts (TP=103,611, TN=54,718, FP=1,282, FN=15,730)
Local SHA-256 computation latency (N=30, mean 5.65 ms, 95% CI: [5.60, 5.70] ms)
In-process EVM contract read latency (N=30, mean 8.90 ms, 95% CI: [8.21, 9.68] ms)
Total pre-load verification gate latency (N=30, mean 20.31 ms, 95% CI: [19.37, 21.30] ms)
Pure off-chain ML inference compute latency (N=100, mean 42.40 ms, 95% CI: [41.25, 43.61] ms)
End-to-end API /predict request latency (N=100, mean 51.49 ms, 95% CI: [50.37, 52.99] ms)
Fail-closed HTTP 503 response and is_loaded == False on tampered and unregistered models
Operational audit log events (10 total recorded, zero raw flow feature payloads persisted)
Zero blockchain queries and zero hash recomputations during /predict calls
derived_measurements: Incremental blockchain pre-load overhead: +14.66 ms mean (+13.82 ms median)
Relative pre-load verification ratio: 3.60x (Config C / Config B)
Pre-load gate to pure inference ratio: 0.48x (20.31 ms / 42.40 ms)
Pre-load gate to end-to-end API request ratio: 0.39x (20.31 ms / 51.49 ms)
Internal deserialization/wrapper overhead in pre-load gate: 6.01 ms
supported_claims: Verification occurs strictly prior to model loading into RAM
The evaluated per-flow inference path performs prediction without a blockchain lookup
Blockchain smart contract adds release authorization and version governance beyond local SHA-256
Fail-closed gate prevents untrusted binaries from populating server memory
Local SQLite database provides operational accountability without decentralized consensus overhead
unsupported_or_untested_claims: Does not prove semantic model safety, absence of backdoor triggers, or data poisoning resistance
Does not protect against adversarial feature perturbations submitted at runtime (evasion attacks)
Does not prove blockchain improves ML intrusion-detection accuracy, precision, or recall
Does not model public Ethereum mainnet gas price spikes, network congestion, or validator reorganizations
Does not demonstrate physical embedded IoT microcontroller deployment (e.g., ARM Cortex-M, ESP32)
Does not constitute a wire-speed packet capture or real-time streaming SLA guarantee
Does not claim universal tamper-proof security if the host operating system is fully compromised
Does not claim SHA-256 prevents arbitrary malicious code execution if an attacker can bypass the gate
limitations: UNSW-NB15 evaluates tabular flow summary vectors, not raw physical NIC packet buffers.
In-process EVM (EthereumTesterProvider) tests smart contract execution without public Ethereum network latency.
SQLite audit store is local and off-chain; it does not claim to be a decentralized consensus ledger.
SHA-256 and ModelRegistry verify artifact integrity and authorization; they do not detect adversarial evasion attacks.
